title: Resolve path ambiguity via filesystem evidence, not string interpretation
context: A POSIX backslash byte in a real filename is indistinguishable from a Windows path separator when looking at the string alone. Blindly normalizing all evidence through toPosixTarget() before the misroute guard saw it caused correctly-homed writes with literal backslash bytes to be falsely refused. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Created guardEvidence() to check the filesystem at decision points: if the raw, un-normalized entry names a real file at root, that settles it (backslash was literal)—keep the raw string and skip toPosixTarget(). Otherwise normalize as before. Scoped only to the three misroute-guard call sites; stored fields continue using centralized normalization.
consequences: Fixes false-positive misroute refusals for files with literal backslash bytes that still exist on disk at the correct root -- the deleted/renamed shape (nothing left on disk to check) needed a follow-up pathKnownToHistory check, added in a later commit on this same branch
Preserves Windows path normalization for the legitimate cross-platform case (files that don't actually exist with backslashes)
Introduces filesystem checks at guard boundaries, trading latency for precision
Makes the misroute guard inherently platform-aware via filesystem reality rather than string patterns
alternatives_rejected: Gating normalization on process.platform: would break Windows-path test coverage and the ~55 other toPosixTarget call sites that have real documented need for cross-platform normalization
Never normalizing paths: would break legitimate Windows-to-POSIX path resolution for git comparison
Always keeping raw strings: would fail to normalize actual Windows paths that don't collide with real POSIX files
